description:
The FSA Vision Track Chainset represents a modern approach to track crank design, combining oversized forged aero crank arms with a 30mm BB386EVO spindle for maximum stiffness and efficiency. Unlike traditional square-taper designs, Vision brings road-derived aero shaping and large-spindle technology to the track, making it one of the stiffest cranksets available today.

Used by Harrie Lavreysen and the Netherlands team, the FSA Vision Track Chainset is trusted by elite riders and popular with those seeking a blend of aerodynamics, rigidity, and modern compatibility, the Vision Track Chainset is an outstanding choice for both sprint and endurance disciplines.

Key Features at a Glance

Forged 6061 alloy aero crank arms
– oversized for rigidity

– ultra-stiff, race-ready design

Why Cranksets Matter in Track Cycling

The crankset is the power transfer hub of your track bike — transmitting every watt you produce to the chain and ultimately the rear wheel. At elite levels, even slight crank deflection can waste watts during 2000W sprint efforts or 4km pursuits. The Vision Track Chainset addresses this with:

Oversized forged aero arms for stiffness and clean aerodynamics

30mm spindle for superior torsional resistance

Accurate 42mm chainline to ensure perfect drivetrain efficiency

For More Information read our article on
Cranksets in Track Cycling: The Overlooked Power Link

Q-Factor & Rider Fit

The Vision Track Chainset features a standard Q-factor optimised for track cycling. This provides:

A narrower stance compared to road cranksets, improving aerodynamics and biomechanical efficiency

Enough width to maintain stability on the steepest velodrome banking

Compared with traditional cranks like Sugino SG75 or Dura-Ace 7710, the Vision offers a more modern aero profile without significantly altering rider stance.

Crank Length Optimisation

The Vision Track is available in 165mm only as this is the standard size for Track Cycling used by all types and sizes of elite Track Cyclist.

Stiffness, Deflection & Materials

Made from solid-forged 6061 aluminium with a 30mm 7050 spindle, the Vision Track achieves extremely high stiffness-to-weight performance. The oversized spindle reduces crank deflection under sprint torque compared to traditional square-taper systems.

While heavier than some carbon alternatives, its aero shaping and rigidity make it one of the most reliable cranksets for high-power output.

Bottom Bracket Compatibility

Designed around the BB386EVO spindle standard

Compatible with all major outboard 30mm bottom brackets

Ensure correct installation for maximum stiffness and minimal bearing drag

Event Suitability

Sprint & Keirin
– ultra-stiff arms resist deflection under peak power

Kilo & 500m TT, Pursuit

– efficient torque transfer with no energy loss

Points, Scratch & Madison
– aero profile complements bunch racing setups

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Does the Vision Track fit all chainrings?
A: Yes, it uses the standard 144 BCD used across all professional track chainrings.

Q: Is this crankset stiffer than Sugino or Dura-Ace?
A: Thanks to the 30mm spindle, the Vision is generally stiffer in torsional resistance, though some riders prefer the traditional feel of square-taper setups.

Q: Which bottom bracket do I need?
A: A BB386EVO-compatible 30mm outboard BB. Options are available for most frame standards.

Q: Is it suitable for Olympic-level racing?
A: Yes. Its stiffness and aero shaping make it competitive at the highest level, it is used by Harrie Lavreysen and the Netherlands team

The 144BCD interface ensures compatibility with all standard track chainrings, including the Sugino ZEN, Digirit, and other performance-focused rings. Combined with a high-quality bottom bracket, the Sugino 75 DD2 supports a clean, consistent chainline, smoother drivetrain engagement, reduced mechanical loss, and a quieter running system when set up correctly.

Whether you are refining your sprint bike, building a reliable training setup, or upgrading your pursuit drivetrain for more efficient power delivery, the Sugino 75 DD2 remains one of the most dependable chainsets in the modern track market.

The crankset is the link between rider and drivetrain — every watt must pass through the crank arms and axle before reaching the chain. Poor stiffness or flex under load wastes watts and can compromise acceleration. The ALDHU solves this with:

Oversized 30mm axle – ensuring torsional stiffness even under 2000W sprint torque

CNC machining & hollow-drilled arms – keeping weight low without sacrificing rigidity

Precision chainline – 43mm, ensure you adjust your setup to match this value

Q-Factor & Pedal Spacing

The ALDHU Track’s narrow Q-factor is optimised for aerodynamics and biomechanical efficiency. Unlike wide road-based cranksets, it supports a tucked position for reduced drag, while still offering the stability track riders need on banking.

Compared to Shimano Dura-Ace 7710 (square taper) and FSA Vision (aero forged arms), the ALDHU offers:

Similar stiffness to Vision (30mm axle)

Lighter weight than both

More customisation via OCP

Stiffness, Deflection & Materials

CNC’d from 7075-T6 aluminium
, with three full-depth drill-outs per arm, reducing weight while maintaining stiffness.

Exceptional stiffness-to-weight ratio
, outperforming most square-taper options and rivalling high-end 30mm spindle cranks.

Designed to minimise crank deflection under high torque, essential for sprint and kilo riders.

OCP Technology – Fine-Tuned Biomechanics

The ALDHU’s OCP (Optimal Chainring Position) mount allows riders to adjust chainring orientation in 1° increments, optimising the point of maximum power transfer. Benefits include:

Improved pedal stroke efficiency

Reduced dead spots

Customisation for sprint vs endurance biomechanics

Q: How does the ALDHU compare to Dura-Ace 7710?

Combined with a high-quality bottom bracket, the Sugino 75 DD2 supports a clean, consistent chainline, smoother drivetrain engagement, reduced mechanical loss, and a quieter running system when set up correctly.
